author: loasngel
quote: Thirteen years. Thirteen years to get a dating simulator. I'm not even joking. I remember exactly where GTA 5 started — a big heist, guns blazing, pure adrenaline. GTA 6 doesn't have to do the same thing, I get that, but what we got instead is "oh, pick up flowers, Lucia will appreciate it" and "oh, don't steal cars in the neighbourhood" and "oh, don't shoot the protestors." You can't do that, you can't be bad, in a game called Grand Theft Auto. Please.Even if you strip out the relationship-simulator stuff, what's left? There's no proper big heist, no funny memorable cutscene, no set-piece that made me lean into my screen. Jason has no personality whatsoever — he's a literal yes-man. "Yeah yeah, oh yeah, hmm, hmm." Even Chop from GTA 5 had more personality. Lucia is just a ****. I can't **** took the realism from RDR 2 — the house building, the small things, the chores — and in RDR 2 those were optional details that added to the immersion. People enjoyed them, some didn't, but they were there. Here you made it the main basis of the game, and now it's just a Sims simulator. You can't expect people who come home tired from a 9-to-5 job to get their dopamine from painting walls. Some might enjoy it, but it's GTA for God's sake. Have we lost the plot?And the ending? Are you serious? I don't even know. It feels like a story written by someone who doesn't know GTA itself to the core. The only thing that actually works is the world — the NPC reactions, the fact that they have their own lives, the graphics, the driving. But honestly, after RDR 2, my expectations were probably too high. This just isn't **** wanted to take a different approach, fine. But you can't forget the audience that built you. I'm not saying I want guns blazing 24/7 or shootouts and heists non-stop. Look at RDR 2 — that was pulp-fiction-level peak writing. Flaws, good, bad, all of it. That's how you write characters. The only thing I'm genuinely excited about now is the online, which is also just a subscription money-making machine at this point. I spent $100 on this game and I can confidently say Rockstar has forgotten who their audience is and how to actually make good games. It's sad. The greatest franchise, gone to dust with this.
